API Reference

Complete reference for the public functions in cube_explorer.api, the GUI-free interface for scripts and notebooks.

Every entry on this page is generated from the function’s own docstring, so it always matches the code. For task-oriented walkthroughs, see the User Guide.

from cube_explorer.api import load_cube, fit_line

Note

cube.wavelength is an astropy Quantity, so it carries its unit. Use cube.wavelength.value when a function or comparison needs plain numbers.

Data Loading

cube_explorer.api.load_cube(filename)[source]

Load a FITS data cube from file.

This function handles multi-instrument FITS files (MUSE, MIRI, NIRSpec) with automatic instrument detection.

Parameters:

filename (str) – Path to FITS file

Returns:

Object containing cube data, wavelength, WCS, and metadata

Return type:

CubeData

Raises:

ValueError – If instrument cannot be detected or file is invalid

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("Level3_ch1-long_s3d.fits")
>>> print(cube.instrument)  # "MIRI"
>>> print(cube.wavelength.shape)  # (1000,)
>>> print(cube.cube.shape)  # (1000, 512, 512)

Region Extraction

cube_explorer.api.extract_pixel_spectrum(cube, x, y)[source]

Extract the 1D spectrum at a single spatial pixel. This is the same lookup the GUI uses; prefer it over indexing cube.cube directly, since it always applies the correct (wavelength, y, x) axis order.

Parameters:

  • cube (CubeData) – Loaded cube, as returned by load_cube()

  • x (int) – X pixel coordinate (0-based)

  • y (int) – Y pixel coordinate (0-based)

Returns:

1D spectrum at (x, y), same length as cube.wavelength

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("data.fits")
>>> spectrum = extract_pixel_spectrum(cube, x=20, y=25)
cube_explorer.api.extract_region_spectrum(cube, mask)[source]

Extract the mean spectrum over an arbitrary spatial region, the same averaging the GUI uses for region selections (each reduces to a 2D boolean mask). Excludes NaN pixels instead of propagating NaN.

Parameters:

  • cube (CubeData) – Loaded cube, as returned by load_cube()

  • mask (numpy.ndarray) – 2D boolean array matching the cube’s spatial shape (cube.cube.shape[1:]); True marks pixels inside the region

Returns:

1D mean spectrum over the masked pixels

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("data.fits")
>>> mask = np.zeros(cube.cube.shape[1:], dtype=bool)
>>> mask[15:35, 10:30] = True  # a rectangular region, [y, x] order
>>> spectrum = extract_region_spectrum(cube, mask)

Gaussian Line Fitting

cube_explorer.api.fit_line(wavelength, spectrum, x1, x2, line_name=None, peak_x=None, header=None, wave_unit=None)[source]

Fit a Gaussian to an emission line in a spectrum. The fitter needs a starting guess for the line center; here it defaults to the brightest sample between x1 and x2, or pass peak_x explicitly.

Parameters:

  • wavelength (array-like) – Wavelength/frequency values. Astropy Quantities are accepted; their units are stripped.

  • spectrum (array-like) – Flux values.

  • x1 (float) – Left boundary of the fitting region.

  • x2 (float) – Right boundary of the fitting region.

  • line_name (str, optional) – Descriptive label for the line. Not stored on the result; it exists for readability at the call site.

  • peak_x (float, optional) – Initial guess for the line center. Defaults to the brightest wavelength between x1 and x2.

  • header (optional) – FITS header used for unit conversion. Pass cube.header to match what the GUI produces.

  • wave_unit (str, optional) – Spectral axis unit, e.g. cube.wave_unit.

Returns:

Object with amplitude, center, sigma, fwhm, area, area_unit, area_native, baseline_slope, baseline_intercept, r_squared, success and message.

area is in erg/s/cm^2 when header is supplied and the cube is in MJy/sr (MIRI, NIRSpec); otherwise it stays in flux*wavelength units. Check area_unit rather than assuming; it always states which. area_native is the unconverted value, which is what you want when dividing by a continuum measured in the cube’s own units.

Return type:

GaussianFitResult

Raises:

ValueError – If no wavelength samples lie between x1 and x2, or if every flux value in that window is NaN.

Example

>>> result = fit_line(
...     wavelength=cube.wavelength,
...     spectrum=cube.spectrum,
...     x1=6.90,
...     x2=6.95,
...     line_name="H2 S(5)"
... )
>>> if result.success:
...     print(f"Line center: {result.center} um")
...     print(f"FWHM: {result.fwhm:.6f} um")

Full-Cube Fitting

cube_explorer.api.create_gaussian_map(cube_data, lam_min=None, lam_max=None, n_jobs=None, **kwargs)[source]

Fit a Gaussian to every spatial pixel’s spectrum in a wavelength window.

This is the same full-cube fitting used by the GUI’s Gaussian mapping dialog. RANSAC outlier rejection is always enabled.

Parameters:

  • cube_data (CubeData) – Loaded cube from load_cube()

  • lam_min (float, optional) – Minimum wavelength for the fit window (default: full range)

  • lam_max (float, optional) – Maximum wavelength for the fit window (default: full range)

  • n_jobs (int, optional) – Number of worker threads (default: auto-detect CPUs)

  • **kwargs – Passed through to fit_gaussians_per_pixel (e.g. fac_above_stdres, noise_min, noise_max, lambda_0, progress_callback)

Returns:

2D parameter maps - ‘amplitude’, ‘center’, ‘sigma’, ‘fwhm’, ‘area’,

’r_squared’, ‘success’, ‘is_detection’, ‘is_upper_limit’

Return type:

dict

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("data.fits")
>>> maps = create_gaussian_map(cube, lam_min=4.65, lam_max=4.70)
>>> print(f"Detections: {maps['is_detection'].sum()}")
cube_explorer.api.export_residual_cube(cube_data, out_path='residual_cube.fits', lam_min=None, lam_max=None, n_jobs=None, return_cube=False)[source]

Fit and subtract a Gaussian at every pixel, writing the residual cube to FITS.

Parameters:

  • cube_data (CubeData) – Loaded cube from load_cube()

  • out_path (str) – Output FITS filename (default “residual_cube.fits”)

  • lam_min (float, optional) – Minimum wavelength for the fit window

  • lam_max (float, optional) – Maximum wavelength for the fit window

  • n_jobs (int, optional) – Number of worker threads (default: auto-detect CPUs)

  • return_cube (bool) – If True, return the residual array instead of writing to out_path – the two are exclusive, not additive: out_path is ignored when return_cube is True.

Returns:

The residual cube if return_cube is True; otherwise None

(the FITS file is written to out_path as a side effect instead).

Return type:

array or None

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("data.fits")
>>> export_residual_cube(cube, out_path="residual.fits", lam_min=4.65, lam_max=4.70)

Continuum Fitting

cube_explorer.api.fit_continuum(wavelength, flux, method='auto', **kwargs)[source]

Fit continuum to a spectrum using automatic peak detection: the same method the GUI uses, detecting emission/absorption peaks and fitting a smooth continuum through the remaining points.

Parameters:

  • wavelength (array-like) – Wavelength/frequency values

  • flux (array-like) – Flux values

  • method (str) – Fitting method - currently only ‘auto’ is supported

  • **kwargs – Additional arguments for fine-tuning: window_size (int): Size of median filter window (default 51, must be odd) sigma_threshold (float): Prominence threshold in sigma (default 2.0) peak_width (int): Minimum width of peaks in pixels (default 1) peak_distance (int): Minimum distance between peaks (default 3) peak_exclusion (int): Pixels to exclude on each side of peak (default 3) iterations (int): Iterative clipping iterations (default 2) smoothing_factor (float): Spline smoothing parameter (default 5)

Returns:

Fitted continuum values matching input wavelength array

Return type:

array

Example

>>> wavelength = cube.wavelength
>>> spectrum = cube.spectrum
>>> continuum = fit_continuum(wavelength, spectrum, sigma_threshold=2.0)
>>> line_only = spectrum - continuum
cube_explorer.api.measure_equivalent_width(fit_result, wavelength=None, continuum_spectrum=None)[source]

Calculate equivalent width (the width of an imaginary rectangular line with the same area) from a Gaussian fit result. A full continuum array is averaged over the wavelengths actually fitted.

Parameters:

  • fit_result (GaussianFitResult) – Result from fit_line().

  • wavelength (array-like, optional) – Wavelength array matching continuum_spectrum. Required when passing a continuum array.

  • continuum_spectrum (array-like or float, optional) – Continuum-only spectrum, or a single continuum level. If omitted, the fit’s own baseline is used.

Returns:

Equivalent width in the same units as wavelength. Returns 0.0 if the fit failed or the continuum level is non-positive.

Return type:

float

Raises:

ValueError – If a continuum array is given without a wavelength array.

Example

>>> continuum = fit_continuum(cube.wavelength, cube.spectrum)
>>> ew = measure_equivalent_width(result, cube.wavelength, continuum)
>>> print(f"Equivalent width: {ew:.6f} um")

Flux Analysis

cube_explorer.api.fit_hitran_lines(wavelength, spectrum, molecule, wavelength_min=None, wavelength_max=None, isotopologue=1, refresh_cache=False, v_upper=None, v_lower=None, header=None, wave_unit=None, continuum=None, contam_catalog=None)[source]

Fit HITRAN spectral lines automatically using database lookup. Same algorithm as the GUI’s Multi-Gaussian Fit: every requested line and any contaminant sharing its chunk fit simultaneously, so they don’t double-claim flux.

Parameters:

  • wavelength (array-like) – Wavelength/frequency values

  • spectrum (array-like) – Flux values

  • molecule (str) – Molecule name (e.g., ‘CO’, ‘H2O’, ‘CH4’, ‘[Fe II]’)

  • wavelength_min (float, optional) – Minimum wavelength to search. If None, uses spectrum min.

  • wavelength_max (float, optional) – Maximum wavelength to search. If None, uses spectrum max.

  • isotopologue (int) – Isotopologue number (default 1 for main isotope)

  • refresh_cache (bool) – Force refresh HITRAN cache (default False)

  • v_upper (int, optional) – Filter by upper vibrational level (e.g., 1 for v=1)

  • v_lower (int, optional) – Filter by lower vibrational level (e.g., 0 for v=0)

  • header – FITS header. Required whenever any line is actually found – each line’s fit width comes from the instrument’s real spectral resolution at that wavelength (MIRI/NIRSpec only), not a guess, so a missing header raises ValueError rather than silently fitting with the wrong width. Also used for the erg/s/cm2 conversion.

  • wave_unit – Wavelength unit string, needed alongside header for the conversion.

  • continuum (array-like, optional) – Pre-fitted continuum, same length as wavelength, subtracted before fitting each line. If None, one is fitted automatically via fit_continuum() – the same fallback the GUI uses when you have not run Automatic Continuum interactively first.

  • contam_catalog (pd.DataFrame, optional) – Non-target lines (a ‘line_wave_um’ column, same format as load_contaminating_lines_catalog()) to give their own component in the fit so they don’t distort a nearby requested line’s amplitude – the same optional catalog extract_flux/Flux Map already supports. None (default) skips this.

Returns:

List of dicts with fit results for each line:

  • wavelength: Fitted line center wavelength

  • species: Molecule name

  • transition: Transition description

  • amplitude: Peak height above the local continuum

  • sigma: Gaussian sigma width

  • fwhm: Full width at half maximum

  • area: Integrated line flux, in the units given by area_unit

  • area_native: Integrated line flux before any CGS conversion

  • area_unit: Units of area – 'erg/s/cm^2' only when header/wave_unit let it convert; always check this rather than assuming

  • r_squared: Fit quality

  • success: Whether fit succeeded

  • message: Status message

Return type:

list

Example

>>> # Fit CO v=1->0 lines only
>>> results = fit_hitran_lines(
...     wavelength=cube.wavelength,
...     spectrum=spectrum,
...     molecule='CO',
...     wavelength_min=4.7,
...     wavelength_max=4.8,
...     v_upper=1,
...     v_lower=0,
...     header=cube.header,
...     wave_unit=cube.wave_unit,
... )
>>> detected = [r for r in results if r['success']]
>>> print(f"Detected {len(detected)} CO v=1->0 lines")
cube_explorer.api.extract_flux(wavelength, spectrum, target_catalog_path, contamination_catalog_path=None, snr_threshold=3.0, continuum_params=None, header=None, wave_unit=None)[source]

Extract total flux by fitting all target lines in a spectrum simultaneously with contaminating lines and continuum; the same algorithm as the GUI’s Flux Map button, run on a single spectrum.

Parameters:

  • wavelength (array-like) – Wavelength values in same units as catalog

  • spectrum (array-like) – Flux values

  • target_catalog_path (str) – Path to target line catalog (ECSV format)

  • contamination_catalog_path (str, optional) – Path to contaminant lines catalog

  • snr_threshold (float) – Minimum signal-to-noise for line detection (default 3.0)

  • continuum_params (dict, optional) – Override the default continuum-fitting parameters (window_size, sigma_threshold, peak_width, peak_distance, peak_exclusion, iterations, smoothing_factor). If None, uses the defaults, which work well for typical spectra.

  • header – FITS header. Required whenever any line is actually detected – each line’s fit width comes from the instrument’s real spectral resolution at that wavelength (MIRI/NIRSpec only), not a guess, so a missing header raises ValueError as soon as a line is found rather than silently fitting with the wrong width. Also used to convert ‘flux’/’contam_flux’ to erg/s/cm2 – ‘flux_unit’ in the result always tells you which you got.

  • wave_unit (str, optional) – Wavelength unit (e.g. ‘um’). Used alongside header for the CGS conversion.

Returns:

Results containing:

  • ’flux’: Total flux, in erg/s/cm2 if header/wave_unit were given and the conversion is supported for this instrument, else native units

  • ’contam_flux’: Total flux attributed to contaminating lines, same units

  • ’flux_unit’: unit of ‘flux’/’contam_flux’

  • ’mean_continuum’: Mean continuum level used for the fit (native units)

  • ’detected_lines’: DataFrame of individual detected line fits

  • ’residuals’: DataFrame of fit residuals

  • ’continuum_curve’: DataFrame of the fitted continuum vs wavelength

Return type:

dict

Example

>>> result = extract_flux(
...     wavelength=cube.wavelength,
...     spectrum=cube.spectrum,
...     target_catalog_path="CO/CO_comprehensive_linelist_with_g.ecsv",
...     header=cube.header,
...     wave_unit=cube.wave_unit,
... )
>>> print(f"Total flux: {result['flux']:.4e} {result['flux_unit']}")
>>> print(f"Detected {len(result['detected_lines'])} lines")
cube_explorer.api.create_flux_map(cube_data, target_catalog_path=None, contamination_catalog_path=None, n_jobs=8, wavelength_min=None, wavelength_max=None, continuum_params=None)[source]

Create a 2D map of target-line flux across the entire data cube: HITRAN CO by default, or a custom target_catalog_path. Same algorithm as the GUI’s Flux Map button (continuum subtraction, then per-pixel fit).

Parameters:

  • cube_data (CubeData) – Loaded cube from load_cube()

  • target_catalog_path (str, optional) – Path to target line catalog (ECSV format). If None, automatically fetches CO from HITRAN.

  • contamination_catalog_path (str, optional) – Path to contaminant lines

  • n_jobs (int) – Number of parallel jobs (default 8)

  • wavelength_min (float, optional) – Min wavelength to fit, and for the HITRAN search when target_catalog_path is None (auto-detect if None)

  • wavelength_max (float, optional) – Max wavelength to fit, and for the HITRAN search when target_catalog_path is None (auto-detect if None)

  • continuum_params (dict, optional) – Override the default continuum-fitting parameters, applied identically to every pixel. If None, uses the defaults, which work well for typical spectra.

Returns:

Map data containing:

  • ’flux_map’: 2D array of flux per pixel, in erg/s/cm2 if cube_data.header supports the conversion (see ‘flux_unit’), else the cube’s native flux unit

  • ’contam_flux_map’: 2D array of contaminating-line flux per pixel, same units as ‘flux_map’

  • ’detection_map’: 2D array with number of detected target lines per pixel

  • ’contam_detection_map’: 2D array with number of detected contaminating lines per pixel

  • ’wavelength’: 1D wavelength array used for fitting

  • ’header’: FITS header from the original cube

  • ’wave_range’: (wavelength_min, wavelength_max) actually used for the fit

  • ’flux_unit’: unit of ‘flux_map’/’contam_flux_map’

Return type:

dict

Example

>>> cube = load_cube("data.fits")
>>> flux_map_result = create_flux_map(cube, n_jobs=4)
>>> print(f"Map shape: {flux_map_result['flux_map'].shape}, unit: {flux_map_result['flux_unit']}")

Rotational Diagram

cube_explorer.api.rotational_diagram(fluxes, flux_errors, molecular_data=None, OPR=None, fit_opr=False, opr_grid=None, fit1T=True, fit2T=False, R=None, dist=4.3204e+20, upper_limits=None, progress_callback=None, molecule='H2', isotopologue=1)[source]

Fit a rotational diagram (1T and/or 2T) to a set of line fluxes. Dispatches to the H2-specific fitter (hardcoded partition function, OPR support) or the general HITRAN-based fitter (any molecule, e.g. CO) depending on molecule.

Parameters:

  • fluxes (dict) – {J: flux_value}, J is the upper rotational level

  • flux_errors (dict) – {J: flux_error}

  • molecular_data (dict) – ‘wavelengths’, ‘Aul’, ‘Eu’, ‘gu’ keys, each {J: value}

  • OPR (float) – Fixed ortho-para ratio (H2 only; ignored otherwise)

  • fit_opr (bool) – Grid-search OPR to minimize chi-squared (H2 only; ignored otherwise)

  • opr_grid (array) – OPR values to search (H2 only). Defaults to np.linspace(0.1, 5.0, 200)

  • fit1T (bool) – Report the 1T fit (always computed regardless, as 2T’s own seed)

  • fit2T (bool) – Perform the 2T fit

  • R (float) – Emitting radius (AU or cm)

  • dist (float) – Distance (pc or cm)

  • upper_limits (dict) – {J: True} for measurements marked as upper limits

  • progress_callback (callable) – (phase, current, total) -> None, for a GUI progress bar

  • molecule (str) – Species being fit, per get_available_molecules()

  • isotopologue (int) – HITRAN isotopologue number for molecule (ignored for H2)

Returns:

Fit results. “OPR”/”OPR_err”/”OPR_err_pos”/”OPR_err_neg” keys

are present only when molecule == ‘H2’

Return type:

results (dict)

Raises:

ValueError – if neither fit1T nor fit2T is True
